clue.text: Main goal: to be relaxed in the shade

indicators.note: letters that are relaxed are loosened from their order and free to settle into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A footballer's chief aim is to take it easy in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be relaxed' rearranges the eight letters of MAIN GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolia is a pale creamy-white colour, a common paint shade named after the flower.

clue.text: Great wave means trouble in front of the ship

indicators.note: the word 'in' places trouble within the front of the vessel; the bow is the forward part of a ship

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
ill means trouble or harm, as in 'ill will'

explanation.surface: A huge wave spells trouble ahead of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is only a link; 'front of the ship' is a single piece naming the forward end of the vessel, not the first letter of 'ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a large rolling wave of the sea, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Arrived, having secured posh car to roll up for tea

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: in a down clue, rolling up reads the word from the bottom upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Someone turns up after getting a smart car to collect them for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to roll up' reverses LIMO to OMIL, which CAME holds ('having secured').
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile is a herbal infusion made from the flowers of the plant, drunk as a tea.

clue.text: Captain's place in game

definitions.meaning: the raised platform from which a ship's captain commands the vessel
a card game for four players in two partnerships

explanation.surface: Where a skipper stands during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's bridge is where the captain stands; bridge is also a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Unruffled tartan worn by chief of clan

indicators.note: the chief wears the tartan, so the cloth is wrapped round the chief's letter

parts.note: a plaid is a tartan cloth worn over the shoulder

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its leading letter

explanation.surface: A calm Highland chief dressed in his clan's tartan.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAID goes round C, the first letter of 'clan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and not easily upset, a synonym for unruffled.

clue.text: Sound boost for man

indicators.note: the clue's first word asks for a word that is said like the next one

parts.note: a fillip is a stimulus or boost

explanation.surface: A solid lift for a fellow's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: FILLIP and the name PHILIP are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip is a man's first name, so a man is an example.

clue.text: Vegetable essence

definitions.meaning: a large green gourd related to the courgette
the innermost or essential part, as in 'chilled to the' core

explanation.surface: The very essence of a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A marrow is a large squash; marrow also means the vital core or essence of something.

clue.text: This the last spoon?

parts.note: a booby prize named after a kitchen utensil is awarded to whoever comes last in a competition

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is the final spoon in the drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: The wooden spoon is the mock prize for finishing bottom, so the word describing that spoon is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The booby prize for last place is a spoon made of timber, so the adjective is what makes it the last one.

clue.text: One may be spoilt for choice in an election

definitions.text: One may be spoilt for choice in an election

parts.words: One may be spoilt for choice in an election
parts.note: voters who dislike every candidate may deface the form they are given, which is called spoiling it

explanation.surface: An election voter is overwhelmed by too many candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt for choice' looks like the idiom for having too many options; here a voting form is literally spoilt as a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The voting slip handed out at a poll is the thing a voter can deliberately invalidate.

clue.text: Aligns malfunctioning warning light

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is not working properly, so its letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A faulty warning lamp lines up the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a light or sign giving a warning or instruction, as on a railway.

clue.text: Secure employment is a piece of luck

definitions.meaning: a fortunate outcome, as in 'it's lucky that happened'

explanation.surface: A steady job counts as good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A good job can be a secure position at work, and the phrase also means a fortunate thing.

clue.text: Girl is both good and bad

parts.note: ill means bad, as in 'ill effects'

explanation.surface: A girl who is both well-behaved and naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Gill is a female first name, an old form of Jill, so a girl is an example.

clue.text: Me always sick? There's a surprise

definitions.meaning: someone permanently poorly could say of themselves 'healthy? I am not, ever'

explanation.surface: A hypochondriac remarks with surprise on being ill all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads the phrase literally: a person who is never healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common exclamation of astonishment, much like 'Fancy that!'

clue.text: Take responsibility for transporting the paint?

definitions.meaning: to accept blame or responsibility for something, often unfairly
literally, lifting and moving the tin that holds paint

explanation.surface: A decorator accepts the job of moving the paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept the blame; read literally it is lugging a tin of paint.

clue.text: Does it make the bank secure?

definitions.text: Does it make the bank secure?

parts.words: Does it make the bank secure?
parts.note: a reef is an underwater bank of rock or sand, and a secure tie is a knot, so this tie might seem to fasten a reef

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something keeps a bank safe from robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests a financial institution; it is a ridge of rock or sand under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A square knot used by sailors for reefing sails, punningly read as fastening a sandbank.

clue.text: Star guide to note

definitions.meaning: the symbol in a text that directs a reader to a footnote

explanation.surface: A celebrity coaching someone to sing the right note.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol * is shaped like a star and is used to point readers to a footnote.

clue.text: If worried, please pass

indicators.note: worried here means shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: An anxious request to be allowed through.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass when it goes by, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Abandon cause that shows flaw

definitions.meaning: to desert one's country or party for another

explanation.surface: Giving up on a campaign reveals a weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to desert a cause; as a noun it is a fault or imperfection.

clue.text: Not stupid about silver being immensely popular

indicators.note: about means around, so the first phrase surrounds the metal's symbol

parts.note: someone 'all there' is mentally alert, not stupid
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A clever person with money is hugely in demand.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL THERE goes about AG, leaving AG between the R and final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the height of fashion means being extremely popular, an idiom.

clue.text: Fool hems in one inexperienced driver in the half-dark

indicators.note: to hem in is to surround, so the fool's letters enclose the others

parts.note: a twit is a silly person
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the learner-driver plate shown in Britain

explanation.surface: An idiot traps a novice motorist at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes something lit only by dusk, the dim light between day and night.

clue.text: Shake down old revolutionary that's turned up

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from the bottom, so it is reversed

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A former revolutionary reappears to run a protection racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake someone down is to obtain money by threats, the same as to extort.

clue.text: Another time in the north

indicators.note: the letters are found in the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: On a different occasion up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside THE NORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means at that time, a time other than now.

clue.text: Spray knocks antelope back after short jump

indicators.note: after says the antelope comes behind the jump
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to spring is to jump

indicators.note: back means the word for the antelope is read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer, loosely used here for an antelope-like animal

explanation.surface: A hunter's spray hits an antelope after a quick leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts SPRING to SPRIN; 'back' reverses ELK to KLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprinkle is to scatter drops or particles, much as one sprays.

clue.text: Artist not following straight career?

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ..., the English landscape painter
someone who turns rather than going straight on

explanation.surface: A painter who strays from a conventional profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner is the famous English painter, and literally one who turns aside.

clue.text: Woman selected from deli, normally

indicators.note: the letters are picked out of the run of text that follows

explanation.surface: A woman chosen from the delicatessen staff, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across DELI and NORMALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor is a woman's first name, as in Elinor Dashwood.

clue.text: Arranged in advance, gift's not new

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the gift

parts.note: a present is a gift; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A pre-arranged gift turns out to be second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Preset describes something set up or fixed beforehand.
